El ejemplo clásico es anterior a la pala: The classic example predates the word by a century and a half. In 1788, James Watt fitted his steam engine with a ball governor: two spheres hanging from a shaft that turns with the engine. If the engine speeds up, centrifugal force opens the balls; on opening, they pull a lever that closes the steam valve; with less steam coming in, the engine slows. And the other way round if it runs slow.

El nombre de esta disciplina, <strong>ci: The name of this discipline, cybernetics, was given by Norbert Wiener in 1948 in a book titled Cybernetics, or Control and Communication in the Animal and the Machine. He took it from the Greek kybernetes, the helmsman of a ship, which is exactly the image: someone who looks at where they are going, sees that they are drifting and moves the tiller. The word “govern” comes from that same root, and so does “governor”, which is what the regulator of a steam engine is called. The vocabulary of politics and that of control engineering are literally the same word.
El precio sube cuando escasea un product: The price rises when a product is scarce, and that rise reduces demand.
El regulador de Watt tiene un papel curi: Watt's governor has a curious place in the history of mathematics: it was the first to resist analysis. It worked, but sometimes the engines began to judder for no apparent reason, and nobody knew why. In 1868, James Clerk Maxwell —the same one of the equations of electromagnetism— published On Governors, in which he set the problem out as a differential equation and proved that stability depended on the signs of the roots of an associated equation. It is the birth of control theory, and it came out of trying to understand why a steam engine got jittery.
El resultado es que el sistema vuelve ha: The result is that the system returns towards its reference value.

En la <strong>realimentación negativa</s: In negative feedback, the correction goes against the deviation: if the result overshoots, the system pushes down; if it falls short, it pushes up. The effect is to stabilise. It is called negative for the sign of the correction, not because it is bad; in fact it is what holds up your body temperature, what keeps the cistern water at its level and what stops a car with cruise control from hurtling downhill.
En la <strong>realimentación positiva</s: In positive feedback, the correction goes with it: the more it deviates, the more it is pushed in that same direction. The effect is to amplify. It is the squeal of a microphone pointed at its loudspeaker, the bank run in which people withdraw money because others are withdrawing it, compound interest and the chain reaction. It is not “bad” either: it is what lets a small decision become a big change.

Ese mando de ganancia es un ajuste real: That gain control is a real adjustment someone has to make on almost any device with a motor. A lift that overshoots the floor and comes back, a 3D printer whose head vibrates and leaves ripples in the part, a drone that wobbles instead of staying still: in all three cases the problem is usually exactly the one in the graph above, too high a gain. And the other way round, a home thermostat with low gain is the one that leaves you cold for half an hour before reacting.
Ese trabajo de Maxwell conecta directame: That work of Maxwell's connects directly with what you already know. The stability condition he found is, in the language of [[av-lineal|linear algebra]], a condition on the eigenvalues of the system: if their real part is negative, the disturbances die away; if it is positive, they grow. The Millennium Bridge and Watt's steam engine fail for the same mathematical reason.
Esta es la misma condición de estabilida: This is the same stability condition we were talking about with Maxwell, in its simplest version: the system is stable if and only if $|1-K| < 1$. In more complicated systems that number becomes several —the eigenvalues— and the condition becomes that all of them stay within a certain limit. But the idea is exactly the one you have just deduced in three lines.

Here the result goes back to the input, and the system bites its own tail. That circularity breaks the usual way of reasoning —who is the cause and who the effect, if each is the other's?— and that is why a new language had to be invented to talk about it.

Correcting harder does not mean arriving sooner and better: past a certain point, the system overshoots, has to come back, overshoots again, and ends up oscillating or running out of control. It is counter-intuitive and it is the most important practical lesson of the topic.

La realimentación negativa es la razón d: Negative feedback is the reason precision devices exist. A motor does not turn at constant speed by itself: it turns at the speed imposed on it by a loop that measures and corrects a thousand times a second. The same thing keeps the frequency of the electricity grid at 50 hertz despite millions of people switching things on and off without warning, and the same thing makes the cursor arrive exactly where you point even though your hand shakes.
La realimentación positiva se estudia me: Positive feedback is studied less and explains more headlines. Its signature is explosive growth, and you already know it under another name: it is the [[fn-exp-log|exponential]], seen from the side of the causes.
La respuesta cabe en una palabra, y es l: The answer fits in one word, and it is the most productive idea of the whole twentieth century in engineering: feedback. A system measures its own result, compares it with what it wanted, and uses the difference to correct itself. Nothing more. With that you explain a thermostat, a cistern, an autopilot, the temperature of your body, the price in a market and a good part of what your brain does when you reach out for a glass.

Wiener era un personaje improbable para: Wiener was an improbable figure to found an engineering discipline. A child prodigy pushed mercilessly by his father, he took his doctorate at Harvard at eighteen in mathematical logic. After the war he flatly refused to go on collaborating with the military: in 1947 he published an open letter, A Scientist Rebels, refusing to work on anything that could be used to kill, and he devoted his last period to warning that deciding machines were going to destroy jobs and to demanding that someone think about it beforehand. His second book is titled The Human Use of Human Beings, and it reads today with an uncomfortable currency.
Wiener llegó a esto por un encargo de gu: Wiener came to this through a war commission. In 1940 he was asked to improve the aim of anti-aircraft guns, and he realised that the problem was not ballistics: it was that the gunner, the gun and the aircraft formed a single system with a loop, and that the same loop appeared in a servomotor and in a person reaching out. Out of that came the thesis that gives the book its title: control and communication are the same thing, and they work alike in the animal and in the machine.
Wiener lo bautizó en 1948 tomando la pal: Wiener named it in 1948 taking the Greek word for helmsman: control and communication are the same thing.
